issue: Circular 230 §10.27 contingent-fee exceptions are stated three different ways. The lesson (L71-77), flashcard reg-c230-f3, reg-c230-02 and reg-x1-21 give the four exceptions correctly. reg-c230-25 says contingent fees are allowed ONLY for interest-and-penalty claims (dropping the 120-day amended-return/refund-claim exception), and TBS reg-tbs-r3-circular230 row a1 attaches the 120-day condition to the examination-of-an-original-return exception, which has no time limit.
evidence: Lesson L73-77: '1. an IRS examination or challenge to an original return; 2. an amended return or claim for refund filed within 120 days after receiving a written notice of examination ...; 3. a claim solely for statutory interest or penalties; 4. a judicial proceeding'. reg-c230-25 (key d) explanation: 'Correct. Contingent fees are allowed only for claims solely for interest and penalties' and item explanation: '§10.27 allows contingent fees for claims solely for statutory interest or penalties, not for tax refund claims.' reg-tbs-r3-circular230 a1 label: '...IRS examination of an original return, with the agreement signed within 120 days of the notice'; explanation: '§10.27 allows contingent fees in connection with an IRS examination of an original return, if signed within 120 days.'
fix: reg-c230-25: add 'No IRS notice of examination has been received' to the stem and rewrite the explanation: 'No. A contingent fee for an amended return or refund claim is allowed only if it is filed within 120 days after a written notice of examination or challenge (or the claim is solely for statutory interest or penalties).' reg-tbs-r3-circular230 a1: drop 'with the agreement signed within 120 days of the notice' from the label and change the explanation to '§10.27(b)(2)(i) allows a contingent fee for representing a client in an IRS examination of an original return; no time limit applies to this exception.' Keep the lesson wording as the reference (optionally add the §7623 whistleblower exception everywhere).

issue: The 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax threshold is stated as a flat $200,000 in the federal-regulation lesson, while the tax modules and both numbers sheets give $200,000 single / $250,000 MFJ / $125,000 MFS (the $200,000 figure is only the employer-withholding trigger).
evidence: reg-federal-regulation lesson L34: 'employees pay an extra 0.9% on wages over $200,000'; L86 insight: 'The additional 0.9% Medicare tax applies only to wages over $200,000 and isn't matched by the employer.' Versus reg-ot-06 ('0.9% × ($300,000 − $250,000)', joint), reg-ot-30 ('threshold is $125,000 for married filing separately'), tcp-numbers L19-20 ('over $200,000 single / $250,000 MFJ / $125,000 MFS; employer withholds over $200,000').
fix: In reg-federal-regulation L34 and L86 say: 'employees pay an extra 0.9% on wages above $200,000 ($250,000 MFJ; $125,000 MFS); employers withhold it on wages over $200,000 and do not match it.'

issue: The AMT character of the ISO bargain element is labelled two ways: a 'preference item' in TBS tcp-tbs-r3-equity-comp and a 'preference-type adjustment' in tcp-x1-35, but an 'adjustment' (§56(b)(3)) in the lesson, flashcard and every other item. Preferences (§57) and adjustments (§56) are separate categories (adjustments can reverse; preferences cannot).
evidence: tcp-tbs-r3-equity-comp row b1 explanation: 'The 30,000 spread is an AMT preference item.' tcp-x1-35 choice c explanation: 'The ISO spread is an AMT preference-type adjustment only.' Versus tcp-stock-compensation lesson L32 'the spread at exercise is an AMT adjustment', tcp-sc-03 '§56(b)(3): the ISO spread is an AMT adjustment', reg-ot-02 'The ISO bargain element is an AMT adjustment at exercise', tcp-x1-07, tcp-sc-f4, tcp-tbs-x1-passive-amt.
fix: Change tcp-tbs-r3-equity-comp b1 to 'The 30,000 spread is a positive AMT adjustment (§56(b)(3)).' and tcp-x1-35 (c) to 'Correct. The ISO spread is an AMT adjustment only (§56(b)(3)).'

issue: The 2026 OBBBA charitable rules are flagged in REG but not in TCP, where the planning content actually spans 2025-2026. REG itemized-deductions (L45) and c-corp-income (L48) note the 0.5%-of-AGI floor, the 35% benefit cap, the $1,000/$2,000 non-itemizer deduction and the 1% corporate floor from 2026; the TCP individual-planning lesson's bunching exercise ('giving $12,000 in 2025 and nothing in 2026') and the TCP bunching items say nothing about them, so the two sections describe 2026 charitable planning differently.
evidence: tcp-individual-planning L96-114: Lee itemizes $20,000 in 2026 under the even-giving plan including a full $6,000 charitable deduction; no 0.5% floor or non-itemizer deduction is mentioned anywhere in content/tcp (search for '0.5%', 'non-itemizer', '$1,000 ($2,000' returns no TCP hits). REG L45: 'Looking ahead to 2026: P.L. 119-21 lets itemizers deduct charitable gifts only to the extent they exceed 0.5% of AGI ... and gives non-itemizers a deduction for cash gifts ... up to $1,000 ($2,000 MFJ).'
source: IRC §170(b)(1)(I), §170(p), §68 as amended by OBBBA §§70111, 70424-70426; review/reference/tax-2025.md §1 and §5
fix: Add the same 'Looking ahead to 2026' note to tcp-individual-planning (bunching section), and add one sentence to the bunching exercise: 'From 2026 the itemized charitable deduction is reduced by 0.5% of AGI, which makes bunching more valuable; a non-itemizer can still deduct up to $1,000 ($2,000 MFJ) of cash gifts.'

issue: The same question (due date of a calendar-year partnership's 2025 Form 1065) is keyed to two different dates. reg-x5-41 keys 'March 15, 2026'; tcp-po-06 keys 'March 16, 2026' because March 15, 2026 is a Sunday. The platform's TBS and numbers sheet also use March 16, 2026. Two REG distractor explanations (reg-x5-39 b, reg-te-10 c) also call 'March 15, 2026' the 1065/1120-S date.
evidence: reg-x5-41: stem 'When is a calendar-year partnership's 2025 Form 1065 due, without extension?' key (c) 'March 15, 2026' — 'Correct. The 15th day of the third month after year-end.' tcp-po-06: same stem, key (a) 'March 16, 2026' — 'Correct. March 15 is a Sunday.' reg-tbs-x5-research rows p and s: 'March 15, 2026 is a Sunday, so the due date moves to Monday, March 16 (IRC §7503).' tcp-numbers L88: 'March 15 (March 16, 2026)'. tcp-tbs-u4-k1 f1 likewise. Calendar check: 15 March 2026 is a Sunday.
fix: reg-x5-41: change choice (c) to 'March 16, 2026' with the explanation 'Correct. The 15th day of the third month; March 15, 2026 is a Sunday, so the return is due Monday, March 16 (§7503).' (or reword the stem to ask for the 'statutory due date (15th day of which month)'). reg-x5-39 (b) and reg-te-10 (c): change the distractor to 'March 16, 2026' or reword the explanation to 'The 15th day of the 3rd month (March 16, 2026, because March 15 is a Sunday) is the Form 1065 and 1120-S date.'

issue: NFP net asset classes are named two ways. Most content uses the ASU 2016-14 classes ('with donor restrictions' / 'without donor restrictions'), and far-nfs-17 and far-nfs-23 even mark 'temporarily/permanently restricted' as eliminated, but the lesson and several items still call the class 'unrestricted net assets' — including the keyed answer text of far-nfs-18.
evidence: far-nfs-18 key (c) text: 'Only in unrestricted net assets' — 'Correct. Expenses decrease unrestricted net assets.' (item explanation: 'net assets without donor restrictions'). Lesson L77: 'Restricted resources "flow through" unrestricted net assets when spent'; L109: 'a release into unrestricted net assets ... net effect on unrestricted net assets is zero'; L128/L133 'unrestricted revenues'. far-nfs-03 (a) and far-nfs-chk1 (d) explanations also say 'unrestricted'. Versus far-nfs-17 (d) 'As temporarily restricted — That category was eliminated.'
source: ASC 958-210-45 / ASU 2016-14 (two classes: net assets with donor restrictions and without donor restrictions)
fix: Replace 'unrestricted net assets' with 'net assets without donor restrictions' in far-nfs-18 (choice c text and explanation), far-nfs-03 (a), far-nfs-chk1 (d) and lesson L77, L109, L128, L133; keep 'unrestricted' only for governmental net position.

issue: The AU-C 505 conditions for using negative confirmations as the sole substantive procedure are listed differently in each place. Only aud-x3-33 includes the requirement that evidence on the operating effectiveness of controls has been obtained; the lesson, flashcard and aud-rev-23 drop it, and the lesson says negative requests are 'used only when' the conditions hold (the conditions govern using them ALONE, not using them at all).
evidence: aud-x3-33 explanation: 'Negative confirmations alone are appropriate when RMM is low and controls are effective, the population has many small homogeneous balances, a low exception rate is expected, and recipients are expected to read them.' Lesson L36: 'negative requests ... used only when RMM is low, there are many small, homogeneous balances, few exceptions are expected, and recipients are expected to read them.' Flashcard aud-ev-f3 and aud-rev-23: same list without the controls condition.
fix: Use one wording everywhere: 'Negative confirmations may be the only substantive procedure for an assertion only if all four hold: (1) RMM is assessed as low and evidence on the operating effectiveness of relevant controls has been obtained; (2) a large population of small, homogeneous balances; (3) a very low expected exception rate; (4) no reason to believe recipients will disregard the requests.' Change the lesson's 'used only when' to 'used as the only substantive procedure only when'.

issue: The disposal deadline for an inherited or gifted financial interest in an attest client is given as 'promptly' in the lesson but 'as soon as practicable (no later than 30 days)' in the TBS. Not contradictory, but the lesson omits the 30-day outer limit the TBS grades on.
evidence: Lesson L25-27: 'the shares must be disposed of promptly (or the senior removed from the team).' aud-tbs-u1-independence row s2: 'Inherited interests avoid impairment only if disposed of as soon as practicable (no later than 30 days after the right to dispose)'.
fix: In the lesson example say 'must be disposed of as soon as practicable, and no later than 30 days after the senior's spouse has the right to dispose of them'.
